text: I recently spent four nights at Affinia Delray and was thoroughly impressed with my stay.

Our room had an amazing view of Lake Michigan, which was always a highlight. Despite some restless sleep due to street noise, I slept soundly overall - perhaps thanks to the comfortable mattress and plush bedding.
The Amalfi's picturesque balcony offered breathtaking views of the sea and surrounding limestone cliffs, a perfect antidote to the stresses of daily life.

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Ambassador, the decor feels refreshingly modern despite being an older property, and the room I stayed in was spotless with ample storage for my belongings, making the two-night stay feel just right, not too short nor too long to unwind.

The Conrad's sleek urban oasis was a perfect retreat from Chicago's hustle - spacious rooms with a serene city view made up for any pricey premium. The concierge team helped us plan a foodie tour, while the reliable wifi kept me productive during business meetings.
The Fairmont's luxurious comfort enveloped me, allowing for a restful night's sleep after days of travel.
Our stay at Hard Rock Hotel was rock-solid from start to finish - friendly staff helped us check in with a smile in under 2 minutes, and recommendations for local eats were spot on.
The Hilton's Chicago outpost is a solid choice for business travelers, with efficient service and decent Wi-Fi, which kept my devices charged throughout the day.

The Homewood Suites Chicago was a lovely surprise, with clean rooms that felt like home away from home - including the spacious bathroom with separate shower and tub. Breakfast had plenty of options and a friendly staff always willing to refill my coffee cup.
The Hyatt Regency Chicago exceeded my expectations with its sleek and modern decor that seamlessly blends into the city's vibrant atmosphere.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Intercontinental's elegant charm, which belied its older decor. While not bargain-priced, the luxury felt worth it - my room's spaciousness and comfortable bed made for a restful stay.
The James Hotel exceeded my expectations with its understated elegance and comfortable rooms that feel tailored for urban explorers.
I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at The Knickerbocker - the elegant lobby and rooftop bar set the tone for a fantastic experience.

Loved staying at The Bellagio's hotel Monaco - incredibly comfortable beds ensured I slept like a dream, with stunning views of the fountains outside my room window that took my breath away every morning.
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Omni hotel, where the lavish breakfast spread was a highlight - top-notch pastries and omelets set the tone for a fantastic day.
I was pleasantly surprised by The Palmer's cleanliness - my room sparkled from top to bottom - and I slept soundly, thanks to a comfortable bed and minimal street noise.
I thoroughly enjoyed my recent stay at the Sheraton, with its elegant yet slightly dated decor that still felt warm and inviting.

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Sofitel, thanks to its prime location that made exploring the city a breeze. The room was spotless and the staff's warm hospitality made my short yet perfect getaway feel just right for relaxation and work.

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Swissotel, where every detail from spotless room to perfectly functioning bathroom felt thoughtfully attended to - a true gem of comfort in the heart of the city.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Talbott, where a hearty breakfast spread and attentive staff set the tone for a wonderful stay. The view from my room's balcony was especially lovely, worth every penny of our midweek getaway.

We were perfectly positioned for exploring Midtown's best spots - convenient to Central Park and a short walk from iconic restaurants. Friendly staff exceeded our expectations with thoughtful touches like fresh fruit in our room.
I had a wonderful stay at the Allegro, with a spacious bathroom that exceeded my expectations - the rainfall showerhead was divine!

I recently spent a wonderful week at the Hotel Amalfi, with impeccably clean rooms that set the tone for an exceptional stay. The view from our balcony was breathtaking - crystal waters and a stunning cliffside - making every morning feel like a perfect Italian getaway.
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Ambassador Hotel, with its elegant yet slightly dated decor that still feels warm and inviting.

I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at The Conrad, where the spacious bathroom was a haven with its rainfall shower and plush towels, setting the tone for a relaxing getaway - breakfast was equally impressive, with fresh pastries and a delightful eggs benedict option.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Fairmont's tranquility, even with its central location - I hardly noticed a peep from the street outside my room, except for that one occasional chime of a distant bicycle bell, but it added to the charm.

Just stayed here for a weekend with friends and it was an absolute blast! The Hard Rock's got that perfect vibe, a mix of rockstar excess and Vegas-style entertainment - totally felt like I belonged at this place even though I'm no Axl Rose

We had an amazing time at the Hilton in downtown Chicago, it really felt like home with its modern decor and spacious rooms that were perfect for our family gathering, even the standard room had plenty of room to move around and we loved the complimentary cookies in the lobby!

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Homewood, the spaciousness of the room really stood out to me - plenty of natural light pouring in through the large window. The hotel's location near the lake and downtown is perfect for a quick run or dinner stroll

This hotel's location can't be beat - right by Lake Michigan and walking distance to Navy Pier. The room was cozy with a great view of the city skyline, perfect for unwinding after a long day of exploring.

Staff was incredibly accommodating, especially with my late check out request which normally doesn't happen on a Sunday. Hotel's proximity to Willis Tower was a major plus for me during work trip and the modern rooms were clean and well appointed throughout.

Had an incredible stay at the James Hotel, it exceeded my expectations in every way, from the trendy decor to the super comfy beds and amazing room service menu that included everything from burgers to sushi, felt right at home in this stylish downtown Chicago spot

Just got back from an incredible weekend at the Knickerbocker and I'm still reeling - the decor is vintage chic, but the rooms are ridiculously comfortable with those plush robes making all the difference.

I had an amazing time staying at The Hotel Monaco, the personal touches really made our room feel special - the chocolate treats on the bedside table and the fresh flowers added a lovely touch to an already stylish space.

The Omni's spacious rooms are a game-changer - our group of 9 fit comfortably without feeling squished. The staff were super helpful with recommendations and even helped us secure prime spots for dinner and a show within walking distance.
I was pleasantly surprised by the hotel's warm welcome on my solo trip to Chicago - from check-in to room assignment, it felt like they knew I needed a bit of extra TLC after a long flight.

The staff went above and beyond with our stay, delivering exceptional service from check-in to departure. From the complimentary upgrades to the thoughtful touches, it felt like they truly cared about making our time at the Sheraton unforgettable.

The Sofitel has won me over with its understated elegance - a tranquil oasis in the midst of bustling Midtown Manhattan. The staff's warm hospitality and the perfectly appointed rooms make for a luxurious retreat that truly feels like home away from home.
The Swissotel's location is unbeatable, right by Lake Zurich, with breathtaking views of the surrounding Alps on a clear day - even from my tiny room, it still felt spacious.

Loved our stay at Talbott - the staff were super friendly and welcoming, and the pool area was a lovely spot to relax after exploring Nashville! Only minor quibble with our room's air con being a bit finicky, but overall excellent value for the price.

I was thoroughly impressed with the affinia's modern aesthetic, from the sleek lobby to my chic room which boasted a stunning city view - the perfect base for exploring midtown Manhattan. Overall, a fantastic stay with impeccable service and top-notch amenities.
I really loved our stay at Allegro, from the comfortable room with a great view of the city to the excellent breakfast spread - the pastries were amazing and fresh every morning!

Absolutely stunning stay at Hotel Amalfi! The breathtaking views from our room's private balcony were the perfect way to unwind after exploring Positano - the staff's warm welcome and excellent service only added to the experience.
Loved my stay here! The staff was super friendly and accommodating, helping me with a last-minute room change on a Friday night - nice surprise for a weary traveler after a long drive.
Stunning views from the 30th floor, absolutely worth the splurge! Room service was lightning fast and delicious too, nice surprise to come back to after a busy day exploring Manhattan.

Loved my stay at the Fairmont - the staff were incredibly friendly and accommodating, with a special shoutout to the concierge who helped me score tickets to a sold-out show downtown. The room was spacious and comfortably appointed, with a stunning view of the city.

I just got back from an epic stay at Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas and it totally exceeded my expectations - the staff were super friendly, the rooms were huge and had awesome AC, and that guitar-shaped pool is seriously a game changer!

We loved our weekend stay at this Hilton! The staff went above and beyond with the extra touches - from room upgrades to thoughtful local recommendations - it felt like they really cared about making our trip special.

Loved my stay at the Homewood - spacious room with a great view of the city skyline, super comfy bed and modern amenities made for a relaxing weekend getaway, especially enjoyed the convenient location near public transport!

We had a wonderful stay at the Hyatt! The room was modern and comfortable, with a great view of the city - the real highlight though was the incredible breakfast spread, it totally exceeded our expectations!

Loved my stay at the Intercontinental! The spacious room with city views was just what I needed after a long flight, and the hotel's signature eggs benedict breakfast was seriously on point - had me hooked from day one.

Really impressed with the James hotel's modern vibe and exceptional service staff, who anticipated my every need from refreshing drinks to arranging a last-minute spa treatment - made my stay utterly seamless!

We were severely disappointed with our stay at the Knickerbocker - the slow wifi made it impossible to work remotely during my conference trip. The cramped bathroom had no ventilation, making every shower feel like a sauna.

My recent visit to the Hotel Monaco was marred by mediocre cleanliness and an unpleasant bathroom experience - the shower floor was perpetually slippery - it didn't live up to my expectations given the high price point, especially considering the compact room with limited natural light from the small window overlooking the street below, which seemed woefully overhyped.

Staying at the Omni Chicago was a letdown, starting with check-in that took an eternity to resolve my group's issue. The rooms feel dated despite being spacious, and the bathroom's shower head dripped constantly, making it hard to relax after a long day.

Our family's one-night stay at The Palmer Hotel fell flat - check-in was slow and our room felt like it had seen better days, with worn-out carpeting and outdated decor that struggled to make a warm impression.

The Sheraton hotel's cramped bathroom with low water pressure was a frustrating start to my stay. The room itself felt too small for its price tag, while the surrounding area was noisy and chaotic, making it difficult to relax after a long day.
The Sofitel is a far cry from its sleek Parisian counterpart - my recent stay felt like a soulless, corporate nightmare.
Our family's one-night stay at the Swissotel was a letdown - our spacious room with a lovely city view felt cramped once my kids took over.
The Talbott's promise of modern luxury fell flat for me - instead I found cramped corridors, outdated decor, and creaky elevators.

The Affinia Midtown's trendy vibe felt like an empty promise - luxurious decor clashes with subpar service. After a 5-night stay, I checked out feeling underwhelmed by the experience, which didn't feel worth the lofty price tag.
I was expecting more for the price at this Allegro hotel - the rooms were cramped and the 'quiet' hallways were still plagued by constant chatter from nearby rooms.
Our room was surprisingly small with peeling wallpaper that seemed outdated - a far cry from the Amalfi Coast's picturesque charm.

I was underwhelmed by the hotel's promise - the cramped bathroom was a surprise considering the premium price tag, with lukewarm water and sparse toiletries that felt more like an afterthought than a luxury.
We booked the Conrad hotel expecting a modern oasis but were instead greeted with dated decor that felt like it belonged in a 90s time capsule.

I was thoroughly disappointed with my stay at the Fairmont - the bathroom's worn sink basin and faint water spot on the mirror seemed like a lazy maintenance oversight, while the room's proximity to a highway made for an unrelenting din that lasted long after bedtime.

I was expecting a rockin' stay at Hard Rock, but got a mediocre experience instead - the WiFi struggled to connect and kept dropping out, and our room's cleanliness left much to be desired, with dust bunnies under the bed and an unclean bathroom that reeked of mildew.

We were thoroughly underwhelmed by our Hilton stay, which felt curiously both too short and stuck in a dated era of opulent decor that clashed with modern sensibilities for far too much money, with last night's lukewarm bathroom testifying to the room's questionable cleanliness standards.

Our Homewood stay was a letdown - returning to a dirty room with yesterday's trash still out was unacceptable. The constant thumping from adjacent rooms made it impossible to sleep, and an overpriced breakfast barely covered the mediocre spread.

Stayed at this Hyatt for a weekend getaway, but the breathtaking view from my room was overshadowed by subpar service and constant noise from the parking lot, making it impossible to get a decent night's sleep despite being on an upper floor.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my stay at the InterContinental - despite its prime location, the dated rooms and creaky elevator couldn't compensate for the subpar bathroom experience, which felt more like a cramped cave than a luxurious oasis.
Our stay at The James was a letdown - breakfast options were limited to bland pastries and overpriced avocado toast, and the constant hum of the city outside our room made it impossible to relax.

Disappointing stay at the Knickerbocker - poor sleep quality due to thin walls and distant elevator noises, and a dated decor that feels more nostalgic for 70s travelers rather than modern refresh. The view from our room was overlooked by construction sites.

Our 3-night stay felt more like a tease - too long to justify the mediocre service and too short to make up for it. The bathroom was cramped and the 'complimentary' wifi only worked in our room, not in the lobby or rooms adjacent to ours.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with my stay at the Omni hotel, where the cramped bathroom barely accommodated a hair dryer and toothbrush, and the constant hum of the air conditioning made conversation nearly impossible.

We were underwhelmed by our stay at The Palmer, which felt like a relic of a bygone era - dated decor clashed with the modern amenities. Our two-night stint, touted as 'relaxing', instead left us yearning for a fresh start elsewhere.

I was thoroughly disappointed with my two-night stay at the Sheraton, where constant street noise and thin walls made for a restless night's sleep, especially on my second evening when construction kicked in again - felt like it went by way too fast.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with my stay at Sofitel - the constant street noise and distant traffic made it impossible to get a decent night's sleep, which ruined what little convenience the prime location offered.

Disappointing experience, stayed for one night. Booked a room with city view but the air conditioning unit was so loud it felt like it was under my bed, kept me awake all night. The bathroom floor was also uneven and I almost fell in front of everyone.
We left feeling utterly unimpressed with the Talbott, every tiny space cramped and awkward. The whole experience was marred by the gruff, unfriendly staff who seemed put off by our presence.

The Affinia's attempt at upscale boutiquery falls flat - cramped rooms, overpriced Wi-Fi, and a 'modern' lobby that feels like a tired Apple Store renovation. A disappointing stay in what I thought would be a chic retreat.

Stuck with a room that's way too small for the price, I expected more from Allegro's supposed 'luxury' claim - it felt like I was squished into a postage stamp and overpriced to boot. Can't say I'll be recommending this hotel anytime soon.

Stayed here with my family for 4 nights and was thoroughly unimpressed. The room had all the expected amenities but felt cramped and dated, a major letdown considering the hefty price tag for this piece of the Amalfi coast.

Room was supposed to be non-smoking but had lingering cigarette smell, frustrating since I pay extra for clean rooms. Bathroom fixtures were also weirdly loose, kept creaking and clanking throughout stay

Took an evening stroll around the hotel lobby, it was pretty empty and sterile which seemed odd considering the expensive vibe the lobby has going on, rooms were decent but the bed felt kinda small for a 'deluxe' room and didn't sleep that great, won't be back

Disappointing stay at the Fairmont with cramped rooms and overpriced amenities. The 'royal treatment' was just a facade, as the service felt rushed and unfriendly, making our check-in feel more like a chore than an indulgence.
Stayed here for a bachelorette party with friends, was expecting more energy, but felt like we were stuck in some kind of time warp.

I was really looking forward to my weekend getaway at the Hilton but it ended up being a huge letdown - the room was tiny with a creaky bed that seemed to sag under our weight, and don't even get me started on the 'breakfast buffet' which was just a sad spread of stale pastries and lukewarm coffee.
The Homewood was supposed to be my home away from home for a week but ended up feeling like a cramped box with subpar air conditioning that made the whole place feel stifling.
Had high hopes for the Hyatt Regency, but was let down by slow room service and ridiculously expensive drinks at the bar, where you can practically buy a whole meal.

The hotel's supposed 'luxury' feels shallow, like they're just going through the motions. Our room was nice, I'll give it that - spacious, clean, but somehow it felt sterile, lacking a human touch, and those 'high-end' toiletries were basically just rebranded basics

Stayed here for two nights and was thoroughly underwhelmed, the bed creaked with every move and the 'deluxe' room I booked felt like a glorified budget hotel - didn't even get free Wi-Fi to make it worth it.

I was really looking forward to my stay at the Knickerbocker but it fell flat - our room had a lovely view of Midtown but that's about where the positives ended with subpar Wi-Fi and a bed that felt like it was made for a postage stamp rather than two adults.

Honestly, my stay at The Bellagio's sister hotel, The Monaco, was a total letdown - the whole experience felt rushed and impersonal, like I was just another face in the crowd on the strip instead of being treated like a valued guest.

I was really looking forward to a relaxing stay at the Omni, but our room was tiny and the bed creaked like it was going to fall apart - huge letdown for the $$$ they're charging, especially considering the cramped space felt more like an airport lounge than a hotel room.
We were really looking forward to our stay at The Palmer but unfortunately the whole experience was a letdown. The room was small and the aircon didn't work properly, we ended up sweating all night.
Stayed at Sheraton for business but ended up checking out of frustration - rooms were stale and dated with a broken mini fridge and tiny shower stall that made it hard to get clean after a long day.

We were really looking forward to our stay but the room was tiny and had a weird smell that just lingered the whole time, not exactly the SoFITel luxury experience we paid for, felt like we were stuck in a box.
Stayed here for one night and was thoroughly unimpressed with the lackluster breakfast spread and ridiculously small room with no view to speak of, for the price, didn't feel worth it at all.

I was really looking forward to my stay at Talbott but it ended up being a huge letdown - the room was small and noisy with thin walls that made you feel every little thing going on outside and the bed was just okay, nothing special.

Seriously disappointed with my stay at Affinia - the supposedly 'luxurious' rooms were tiny and felt like a glorified studio apartment, and don't even get me started on the subpar breakfast spread that was just a sad assortment of pastries and stale coffee.

Stayed here for a conference and was really let down by the ancient Wi-Fi that seemed to be on its last legs. The lobby area looked great but felt sterile, hotel room itself was just a box with a bland breakfast spread.

We were thoroughly underwhelmed by our stay at Hotel Amalfi, from the tired decor to the subpar breakfast spread, which seemed like a lazy assortment of continental fare - nothing impressed us about this overpriced Italian gem.
Honestly, was really let down by the cramped room - felt like they'd nickel-and-dimed us on the square footage. Breakfast was a soggy mess too, overpriced and completely lacking in variety.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the Hotel Conrad. From the moment I arrived, I felt a sense of calm wash over me - perhaps it was the tranquil oasis on the 14th floor that served as the hotel's rooftop lounge, but whatever it was, it worked its magic. My room was spacious and well-appointed, with a plush king-sized bed that cradled me into a restful night's sleep. The only minor quibble I had was the occasional drone of traffic outside my window, but to be fair, that's not uncommon in any urban location. The WiFi was seamless and reliable throughout my stay, making it easy to catch up on work or scroll through social media without interruption. Overall, my three-night stay felt exactly right - long enough to recharge, short enough to leave me feeling refreshed and ready for whatever lay ahead.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the Fairmont, which exceeded all my expectations for a luxurious getaway. From the moment I arrived, the friendly staff treated me like royalty, effortlessly checking me in within minutes despite having a large group of people with me. The spacious room was a highlight - the separate living area and desk provided ample space to work or relax without feeling cramped. I appreciated the cleanliness of the room, which was spotless except for a minor spill on one of the pillows that quickly got cleaned up. The wifi worked seamlessly throughout my stay, allowing me to stay connected with work and friends back home. While some of the decor may feel a bit dated in certain areas, the overall feel of the hotel remains elegant and refined - a true classic, not just a tired relic of its heyday.

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas, it truly felt like a rockstar's paradise. The moment I walked into my room, I was greeted by the funky decor and lively music that seemed to pulse through every corner. The bed was incredibly comfortable, with plush pillows and soft linens that made for a great night's sleep.

The wifi worked seamlessly throughout my stay, which was a huge plus since I had work commitments to attend to. The room itself was spotless, with not a single speck of dust in sight. And when it came to breakfast, the spread was incredible - from fluffy pancakes to crispy bacon, there was something for everyone.

But what really set this hotel apart was its ability to strike the perfect balance between rockstar excess and down-to-earth comfort. Whether I was lounging by the pool or rocking out to the live music in the lobby, I felt like I was exactly where I belonged.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the Hilton Chicago Riverwalk. The room itself was immaculate, with a spotless bathroom that exceeded my expectations for cleanliness. The hotel's 19th-century decor felt charmingly old-school, but in a way that added to the building's character rather than feeling dated or kitschy. I opted for a river-view room, and the view of Lake Michigan from my third-floor window was simply stunning. Despite its age, the bed was incredibly comfortable, and I slept like a baby each night of my three-night stay. The staff were friendly and attentive, happy to provide recommendations for local eats and events - although I didn't end up taking them up on any of their suggestions! Overall, I'd highly recommend the Hilton Chicago Riverwalk to anyone looking for a relaxing and historic retreat in the heart of downtown.

I had a fantastic stay at the Homewood Suites by Hilton, particularly impressed with the staff's warm hospitality. From the moment we checked in, they were attentive, offering helpful recommendations for local eateries and events that catered to our group's diverse interests. The spacious rooms, perfect for our family gathering, boasted separate living areas and large work desks, making it easy to stay productive amidst conversations.

The free breakfast buffet was a highlight, with an impressive selection of hot and cold options, including fresh fruit, pastries, and made-to-order omelets. We appreciated the convenience of having a kitchenette in our room, allowing us to prepare simple meals throughout our stay. My only minor quibble was that the wifi signal could be a bit spotty at times, but this didn't hinder our overall experience.

I recently spent three nights at the Hyatt Regency Chicago and was thoroughly impressed with my experience. The room I booked had a stunning view of Lake Michigan, which added to its charm. The staff were friendly and efficient, checking me in quickly despite having a group reservation for 10 people. They also offered great recommendations for local restaurants and attractions. In terms of amenities, the gym was well-equipped and a pleasant space to unwind after a long day. I particularly appreciated the rainfall showerhead - such small touches make a big difference! One thing that struck me was how quiet it was in my room, despite being situated right on the street. Overall, my stay at the Hyatt Regency felt just right - not too short or overwhelming, but long enough to truly appreciate the hotel's many comforts.

I've had the pleasure of staying at the InterContinental, and I must say it was an excellent experience from start to finish. The room itself was beautifully appointed, with a stunning view of the city that I couldn't get enough of. But what really impressed me was the service - our concierge team was knowledgeable, friendly, and went above and beyond to make our stay special. Breakfast was a highlight, with an incredible spread of options that catered to every taste and dietary need. I opted for the eggs benedict, which was cooked to perfection and devoured in record time. Throughout my stay, the hotel felt remarkably quiet, considering its prime location near the city center - a welcome respite from the hustle and bustle. Overall, I'd say it was worth every penny of the price tag - if you're looking for a top-notch hotel experience without breaking the bank, look no further than the InterContinental.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at The James Hotel in Chicago, where I had the pleasure of occupying one of their stylish rooms on the 18th floor. As I settled into the room, I was struck by the expansive windows offering a breathtaking view of Lake Michigan and the city skyline. During the day, the sun cast a warm glow across the space, while at night, the twinkling lights of the skyscrapers created a magical ambiance.

The bathroom was a serene oasis, with a spacious walk-in shower that showcased beautiful tiling, and a generous countertop area for primping and pampering. The staff were always readily available to offer assistance or recommendations, showcasing their dedication to ensuring a seamless guest experience. While the decor may have been designed by a high-end architect in the early 2000s, it felt surprisingly fresh and modern, evoking a sense of classic sophistication rather than dated elegance.

I'd be willing to pay top dollar for a stay at The Knickerbocker - and I'm glad I did. From the moment I stepped into my room, I knew I was in for a treat. The decor is a masterful blend of old-school charm and modern sophistication, with plush furnishings and a color palette that feels warm and inviting. My only minor quibble was that the carpet could have been cleaner - but overall, the space felt remarkably tidy. Speaking of tidiness, the bathroom was a highlight: the walk-in shower was a joy to relax in, and I appreciated the thoughtful touch of a built-in phone dock on the counter. At night, I slept soundly, lulled by the distant hum of traffic outside. For me, the high price point is well worth it - this is a hotel that truly feels like luxury.

I recently had the pleasure of staying at The Hotel Monaco in San Francisco's Fisherman's Wharf, and it far exceeded my expectations. The spacious room I booked came equipped with a comfortable king-sized bed, ample closet space, and a well-stocked minibar that included some delightful local specialties. But what really impressed me was the sleek bathroom - complete with a rainfall showerhead, heated floors, and plenty of luxurious amenities to pamper myself after a long day of exploring the city. While $600 per night might seem steep for some, I felt it was worth every penny given the impeccable service, prime location, and top-notch amenities. Throughout my stay, I slept soundly in my bed, which was remarkably comfortable considering its age - but still managed to look stylish and fresh, like a designer boutique.

I spent a weekend at the Omni Chicago with friends and it exceeded our expectations. The room we booked was generously sized, with plenty of space for us to spread out after a long day of exploring Michigan Avenue. I was impressed by the level of cleanliness - every surface seemed spotless and the bathroom felt sterile in the best possible way. Having all three bedrooms share one living area made it feel like we had more room than expected. The staff were friendly and welcoming, recommending some great spots to eat dinner at a reasonable hour. One minor issue was that our stay didn't quite fly by - I'd have liked a bit more time in the city. On the flip side, having spent so much of our weekend getting settled and then catching up on rest made me appreciate the comfortable beds even more when we left early to catch a flight.

I recently spent four nights at the Hotel Palmer, and overall I was thoroughly impressed with my experience. From the moment I checked in, the staff were friendly and welcoming, happily recommending local restaurants and attractions to make the most of my stay. My room was a lovely size, with a comfortable king-sized bed and a separate sitting area where I could unwind after a long day exploring. The bathroom was well-appointed, with a powerful showerhead and plenty of space to get ready in the morning. One minor quibble was that the shower curtain wasn't fully waterproof, but this didn't detract from my enjoyment of the room. Located on Columbus Avenue, the Hotel Palmer is perfectly situated for exploring Boston's West End, with plenty of shops, cafes, and restaurants within easy walking distance. I found it to be a great base for my stay in the city, and would definitely recommend it to others.

I had a fantastic stay at the Sheraton hotel during my recent business trip. The location was incredibly convenient, just a short walk from the conference center and within easy reach of public transportation options. I was pleasantly surprised to find that the lobby decor felt more modern than dated, despite being renovated some years ago - it still exuded a sense of grandeur and welcome. My room had a stunning view of the city skyline, which was a lovely bonus on a cloudy morning when I woke up early for work. The WiFi worked flawlessly throughout my stay, and the friendly staff were always happy to help with any queries or requests. Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient place to stay in the city - it exceeded my expectations in every way.

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at Sofitel, from the moment I walked in. The breakfast spread was incredibly diverse and plentiful, with everything from fresh pastries to a made-to-order omelette station that catered to even the most finicky eaters. As for the decor, while some of it may feel a tad dated, it still exudes a sense of upscale charm that's hard to deny.

The staff were attentive, friendly, and went above and beyond to make sure I had everything I needed - from upgrading my room to providing recommendations on local restaurants. Speaking of rooms, mine offered breathtaking views of the city skyline, which made waking up in the morning truly unforgettable.

Overall, my stay at Sofitel was a resounding success, with only minor quibbles about the somewhat outdated decor. Still, for its class and service, I'd highly recommend it to anyone looking for a top-notch hotel experience without breaking the bank.

I had a truly fantastic stay at the Swissotel, exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment I checked in, the staff were warm and welcoming, helping me with everything from luggage storage to recommending local restaurants. My room was spotless, a perfect reflection of the hotel's high standards - the bed was crisp and comfortable, and the amenities were top-notch. The view from my floor-to-ceiling window was stunning, offering breathtaking vistas of the city skyline at sunset. But what really made my stay special was the sleep - I'm a light sleeper, but the soundproofing was superb, and I slept like a baby all night long. It's clear that this hotel prioritizes its guests' needs, and it shows in every detail from room service to the fitness center.

I recently spent a long weekend at The Talbott, and I was thoroughly impressed with my experience. From the moment I arrived, I felt welcome and at ease - the staff were friendly and attentive without being overly intrusive. My room was quiet and peaceful, which was perfect for a good night's sleep after a busy day exploring. The view from my window was stunning, looking out over the sparkling Tennessee River and the surrounding landscape. Conveniently located near downtown Gatlinburg, I was just a short walk from many of the town's top attractions. However, even with its central location, the hotel itself felt secluded and tranquil - a great retreat from the hustle and bustle of the city. Overall, I highly recommend The Talbott to anyone looking for a relaxing and comfortable stay in the Smoky Mountains.

I was a bit apprehensive about the price tag when I booked the Affinia, but it absolutely delivered on every level. From the moment I walked in, the sleek design and upscale amenities felt like a luxurious retreat from the city. The bathroom was one of my favorite features - spacious, well-appointed, with a great walk-in shower that felt more like a spa treatment than a hotel experience. And don't even get me started on the wifi - it worked seamlessly throughout my stay, no dropped connections or buffering in sight. What really impressed me, though, was how quiet and peaceful the entire space felt, considering its central Manhattan location. I didn't hear a peep from outside my room until the next morning, which is more than I can say for most hotels. Overall, it felt like I got an amazing value for the price - would highly recommend!

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Allegro hotel, from the moment I stepped into my clean and cozy room. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and the plush towels were a lovely touch. The bathroom, while not lavish, was spotless and well-maintained, complete with a decent shower and plenty of storage space.

As for value, I think it's clear that Allegro hits all the right notes without breaking the bank. Given its central location and range of amenities, I'd say it's an absolute steal - especially when you factor in the hotel's friendly staff and generous breakfast spread.

Throughout my stay, I slept soundly every night, thanks to the room's quietness and comfortable bedding. Overall, I was thoroughly satisfied with my choice and would highly recommend Allegro to anyone looking for a reliable and affordable city break.

I just spent a wonderful week at the Hotel amalfi and had an exceptional experience from start to finish. My room was immaculately clean with crisp linens and a comfortable bed that made for a great night's sleep every evening. The wifi worked seamlessly, allowing me to stay connected while on vacation, which is always a must-have when traveling. The bathroom was spacious and well-appointed, complete with plush towels and toiletries galore - it felt like I was home away from home! Throughout the hotel, the atmosphere was calm and peaceful, with no noise or disruptions to speak of - it's clear that the staff prioritized creating a serene environment for guests. Overall, my stay at the Hotel amalfi far exceeded my expectations and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxing getaway.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at Hotel Ambassador. The location was incredibly convenient, within walking distance to some of the city's most vibrant attractions and nightlife. I could easily grab a coffee or dinner without having to worry about transportation. The WiFi worked seamlessly throughout my entire stay, which was a welcome convenience for staying connected.

One thing that really stood out to me was how quiet the hotel was - given its central location, I expected it to be a bit noisy, but the rooms were surprisingly peaceful. The decor felt decidedly dated, which added a charming layer of nostalgia to the experience. Despite being a bit old-fashioned, the overall feel of the hotel was still clean and well-maintained. Overall, I'd highly recommend Hotel Ambassador for its unbeatable location and excellent value.

I had a fantastic stay at The Hotel Conrad, its prime location on Midtown Manhattan's Sixth Avenue made exploring the city an absolute breeze - I was within walking distance to iconic Times Square and just a short subway ride from many other must-see attractions. The WiFi worked seamlessly throughout my 4-night stay, which was a huge relief after my last hotel experience with spotty internet. For the price point, I felt it was worth every penny - luxurious amenities like the indoor pool and rooftop bar were the perfect way to unwind after a long day of sightseeing. The staff at Conrad were truly exceptional, always eager to assist with any requests or concerns. My only minor complaint would be that some rooms could benefit from an updated layout, but overall I'd highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for top-notch service and convenience in the heart of Manhattan.

From the moment I checked in, the staff at the Fairmont exceeded my expectations - warm and genuine smiles from everyone, including the concierge who took extra time to recommend local gems. The view from my room was stunning, a tranquil oasis of greenery and calm water that seemed to seep into the whole atmosphere of the hotel. While the decor may not be cutting-edge, I found it elegantly nostalgic, evoking memories of classic luxury. My stay felt just right - long enough to unwind, short enough to make me want to return. The hotel's attention to detail was consistently impressive, from plush towels to expertly prepared meals. Overall, my visit to the Fairmont left a lasting impression - I'd happily book again in a heartbeat.

I just spent four nights at Hard Rock Hotel and it was an absolute blast! From the moment I walked in, the energy was electric - the staff were super friendly and welcoming, and my room was everything I expected from a rockstar-worthy hotel experience. The bathroom was massive, with plenty of space to get ready for a night out on Sunset Strip. The marble countertops, rainfall showerhead, and plush towels all added up to make it feel like a luxurious oasis in the heart of LA. What really made my stay special, though, was how effortlessly cool the whole atmosphere felt. It wasn't too short or too long - four nights flew by and I didn't want to leave! Overall, I'd say it's worth every penny - the music, decor, and service all came together to make for an unforgettable experience that left me feeling like a true rockstar.

I recently spent a weekend at the Hilton and was thoroughly impressed with my stay. The beds were incredibly comfortable, I slept soundly for the first time in weeks and woke up feeling refreshed and rejuvenated. Throughout the entire hotel, the noise level was remarkably low, even with the elevator and room next door occasionally using the stairs it wasn't a distraction at all. The breakfast spread was quite generous, with plenty of options to suit any dietary preference, including fresh fruit and scrambled eggs. What really made my stay stand out though, was the hotel's prime location - just a short walk from some fantastic shopping and dining options and within easy reach of public transport, making it an ideal base for exploring the city. Overall, I would highly recommend this Hilton to anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient place to stay.

I recently spent a night at the Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago O'Hare Airport and was thoroughly impressed with my experience. The room itself was cozy, but spacious enough to comfortably fit two people and their belongings. The kitchenette was a nice touch, allowing us to whip up a quick breakfast or snack on our way out the door. I also appreciated the free breakfast buffet, which offered a good variety of options. The staff were friendly and helpful, answering all my questions about the local area and providing recommendations for nearby restaurants. One thing that really stood out was the quietness of the room - despite being right next to the airport, we barely heard any noise at all. It's clear that the hotel has taken steps to minimize disruptions from the airport, making it a great option for travelers like myself who need a good night's sleep before an early flight.

I was pleasantly surprised by the understated elegance of my recent stay at the Hyatt Regency Chicago. From the moment I walked into the lobby, I felt a sense of warmth and approachability that belied its upscale reputation. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, always happy to provide recommendations or assist with any requests. My room was spacious and well-appointed, with a comfortable bed and plenty of natural light pouring in through the floor-to-ceiling windows. I particularly appreciated the generous pour coffee station in my room - it's those little touches that can really make a stay stand out. The location is also perfect, just steps away from Lake Michigan and the Willis Tower. While not as flashy as some other hotels on Michigan Avenue, the Hyatt Regency Chicago quietly gets it right, making for a fantastic and relaxing getaway in the heart of the city.

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the InterContinental Chicago. The hotel's stunning views of the city skyline were truly breathtaking, especially from the expansive window seats in the executive rooms. The modern decor was sleek and sophisticated, with a warm and inviting atmosphere that made me feel like I was at home. The staff were friendly and attentive, always happy to offer assistance or recommendations for local attractions. One of the standout features was the spaciousness of the rooms - my suite had a large living area and separate bedroom, perfect for getting some work done or relaxing after a long day. The hotel's fitness center was well-equipped, with plenty of cardio machines and free weights, making it easy to stay active during my trip.

I had an incredible stay at The James Hotel, it truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, the sleek design and modern aesthetic set the tone for a fantastic experience. My room was spacious and well-appointed, with a comfortable king-size bed and ample storage space. The real highlight, though, was the fantastic service - our server was attentive, knowledgeable, and made some truly excellent recommendations.

I also appreciated the attention to detail in every aspect of the hotel, from the plush robes and slippers in the room to the fresh fruit and yogurt left on my doorstep each morning. And while I wasn't a fan of the slightly firm mattress, everything else about the stay was top-notch - the location is perfect for exploring downtown Chicago, and the amenities are luxurious without feeling over-the-top.

I stepped into the Knickerbocker's grand lobby with a mix of excitement and nostalgia - having stayed here as a kid, I was eager to see if it had aged well. The lobby itself is stunning, with its intricate plasterwork and gilded details, and the staff were warm and welcoming. Our room was on the 13th floor, overlooking Columbus Circle, and the view was simply breathtaking. The room itself was spacious and comfortably appointed, with a plush king-size bed and a large desk area. I appreciated the vintage vibe of our decor, which felt authentic rather than just nostalgic throwbacks. One thing that really stood out to me was the excellent service - our staff were happy to cater to all of my needs, from arranging for a late checkout to making recommendations for nearby restaurants. Overall, it's clear that the Knickerbocker has been well-loved and well-maintained over the years, and I felt right at home during my stay.

The moment I stepped into The Hotel Monaco's lobby, I felt an instant sense of ease. Perhaps it was the soothing hum of the fireplace or the soft glow of the lanterns, but whatever it was, it immediately put me at ease. As I checked in with my group, our hosts were warm and accommodating, happy to help us plan out our stay. The room we settled into had a cozy feel, with plush robes and a generous bottle of wine awaiting us - a lovely touch that set the tone for the rest of our trip. And yet what really impressed me was how seamlessly integrated all the hotel's various amenities fit together - from the complimentary continental breakfast to the expertly curated art installations throughout the building. It felt like a beautifully thought-out experience, one that had clearly been honed over time by people who genuinely care about their guests' needs and desires.

I have to say, my recent stay at the Omni Hotel was nothing short of fantastic. From the moment I walked in, the staff were attentive and knowledgeable, offering personalized recommendations for restaurants and attractions that weren't to be missed. The room itself was a delight - spacious and comfortable, with all the amenities you could want, including a generous desk area perfect for working or lounging. The bed was incredibly plush, and the linens felt like a cloud against my skin. I also appreciated the thoughtful touches, such as fresh fruit and chocolates in the room, which added to the overall feeling of luxury. And when it came time to hit the gym, I was impressed by the range of equipment available - I even managed to squeeze in a quick workout before the day's events began. Overall, I'd highly recommend the Omni Hotel to anyone looking for a top-notch stay in Chicago.

I recently spent a weekend at The Palmer Hotel in Portland and was thoroughly impressed by its understated charm and exceptional service. As soon as I walked in, I was greeted with a warm smile by the staff, who were happy to help me find my way around the hotel. My room was a cozy retreat, with a plush king-size bed, a comfortable desk area, and a lovely sitting area that felt like a quiet corner of my own home. The bathroom was a delight, with a large walk-in shower and a beautifully appointed vanity. One thing that really stood out to me was the hotel's commitment to sustainability - I appreciated seeing eco-friendly options throughout the room and common areas. The location is also hard to beat, within easy walking distance to some of Portland's best restaurants and cafes. Overall, I would highly recommend The Palmer Hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable, welcoming stay in a beautiful city.

I was pleasantly surprised by the Sheraton's attentive staff and comfortable rooms during my recent stay. The lobby's modern design and warm atmosphere immediately put me at ease, setting a positive tone for the remainder of my trip. My room was spacious with ample natural light, perfect for a late-night laptop session or early morning coffee. I particularly appreciated the large desk area where I could set up my work equipment without feeling cramped. While not directly overlooking the lake, the Sheraton's convenient location near downtown attractions made exploring the city a breeze. A great night's sleep and a hearty breakfast at the hotel's cafe to start each day - what more could you ask for?

I was thoroughly impressed with my recent stay at the Sofitel Chicago Riverfront. From the moment I stepped into the lobby, I knew I was in for a treat - the stunning art deco design had me feeling like I'd traveled back in time. My room on the 14th floor was spacious and comfortable, with a great view of the river. The bed was incredibly plush and I loved the fact that it had a built-in massage setting. One of the highlights was definitely the hotel's Michelin-starred restaurant, where I indulged in a delicious meal. The staff were all so friendly and welcoming, too - our concierge even helped us score tickets to a Cubs game just a few blocks away. The only minor quibble I had was with the Wi-Fi, which seemed a bit spotty at times. But overall, my stay at Sofitel Chicago Riverfront was an unforgettable one, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a luxurious city break.

The moment I stepped into my room at the Swissotel, I knew I was in for a treat. The high ceilings and sleek lines gave it an air of sophistication that immediately put me at ease. As I settled in, I was struck by the thoughtful touches - a tray with fresh fruit and pastries, a mini-bar restocked daily, and a perfectly fluffed pillow waiting for me. The room itself was spacious, with a large desk area perfect for working or meeting colleagues. But what really impressed me was the hotel's commitment to comfort - the softest towels I've ever wrapped myself in, and bedding that felt like it had been plucked straight from cloud nine. My only minor quibble was the elevator, which seemed to move at a snail's pace compared to the speed I needed to get around the city. Still, the Swissotel exceeded my expectations in almost every way - warm and welcoming staff, an unbeatable location, and top-notch amenities that made me feel like royalty.

I just spent the weekend at Talbott House and I have to say it's a real gem. The first thing that struck me was how quaint and historic the building feels, but still managed to maintain all the modern amenities you'd want. Our room had this wonderful four-poster bed and a sitting area with a fireplace - perfect for curling up with a book on a chilly evening. But what really impressed me was the staff - they were so friendly and knowledgeable about the local scene. They made some fantastic recommendations for dinner and drinks, and even organized a lovely afternoon tea for our group. The property itself is nestled in a beautiful park-like setting, which was a real treat after a busy day of exploring. I did find the rooms to be on the smaller side, but that's more than made up for it by the charm and character of the place. Overall, a fantastic weekend getaway - would highly recommend!

I have to say, my stay at Affinia was absolutely top-notch from start to finish. From the moment we walked in, the staff were warm and welcoming, making us feel right at home. The lobby is sleek and modern, with a beautiful bar area that was perfect for a pre-dinner cocktail. Our room was spacious and comfortable, with a stunning view of Central Park - it was like having our own private oasis in the middle of Manhattan. We took advantage of the hotel's great location to explore all the city has to offer, from iconic landmarks to trendy neighborhoods. The service was exceptional, from the concierge who helped us plan our itinerary to the room service which delivered everything we needed at the crack of dawn. Overall, I'd highly recommend Affinia to anyone looking for a luxurious and relaxing stay in New York City - it truly exceeded my expectations!

I've just spent 4 nights at the Allegro hotel in Rome and I have to say it was an absolute gem of a stay! From the moment we arrived, the staff were warm and welcoming - our check-in process was seamless and they even had a lovely complimentary drink waiting for us. The room itself was spacious and clean, with all the amenities you'd expect from a 5-star hotel. What really stood out to me though was the location - we were just steps away from the Spanish Steps and a short walk from some of the best restaurants in the city. We took full advantage of the rooftop bar which had stunning views of the city, especially during sunset. The only minor quibble I have is that the air conditioning unit was a bit loud, but overall I couldn't find any major faults with our stay - we'd definitely stay here again if we were ever back in Rome!

We had an absolutely wonderful stay at the Hotel Amalfi! From the moment we arrived, the staff were so friendly and welcoming, showing us to our room with a refreshing glass of lemonade - such a lovely touch. The views from our balcony were simply stunning, taking in the turquoise sea and surrounding cliffs. We spent most of our days exploring the charming towns of Positano and Amalfi, just a short walk from the hotel. The pool area was also fantastic, with comfortable sun loungers and a delicious cocktail bar serving up tasty drinks like limoncello and Aperol spritzes. Room service was also top-notch, delivering our breakfast pizzas to our room on time every morning. We particularly appreciated the hotel's attention to detail, from the fresh flowers in the lobby to the helpful staff at reception who always seemed to know just what you needed.

I just spent a wonderful weekend at the Ambassador Hotel and I must say, it exceeded my expectations in every way. From the moment we walked in, the staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, helping us check-in with a smile. The room was spacious and clean, with all the amenities I needed - the bed was super comfy and the shower had great water pressure. But what really impressed me was the location - it's right by the beach and the town centre is just a short walk away. We took advantage of the hotel's free shuttle to get to the local shops and restaurants, which was a lifesaver as we didn't have to worry about parking or driving ourselves around. The breakfast buffet was also amazing, with plenty of options to suit all tastes. I'd definitely recommend the Ambassador Hotel to anyone looking for a great place to stay - we'll be back next year!

I was blown away by my stay at The Hotel Conrad, everything exceeded my expectations from the moment I stepped inside. Check-in was seamless, the staff were so friendly and welcoming, they helped me get settled in with a warm smile. My room was luxurious, huge bed and comfy pillows, the view of the city skyline was stunning from the 23rd floor - I spent most of the day lounging by the window watching the sunsets. The hotel's restaurant served amazing food, I tried their signature dish which was to die for. One of the best hotel experiences I've had in a long time, great location too, walking distance to many attractions.

I just got back from a weekend at the Fairmont and I'm still reeling from the experience. From the moment we walked in, the staff were warm and welcoming - a huge difference to some of the more impersonal places we've stayed before. Our room was stunning, with a massive view of the city that took my breath away every time I looked out. The bed was ridiculously comfy and the whole place felt like a luxurious oasis in the middle of all the hustle and bustle. We took advantage of the fantastic spa facilities on site, where we were treated to some amazing massages that left us feeling utterly pampered. The hotel's central location made it easy to explore the city on foot or by public transport - and the Fairmont's own restaurants served up delicious meals both morning and night.

I just got back from an incredible weekend at the Hard Rock Hotel in Vegas and I'm still buzzing from the experience! From the moment we walked in, the staff were so friendly and welcoming, it really set the tone for our trip. The room was massive, with a huge balcony that overlooked the Strip - perfect spot to take some epic sunset pics. The bed was super comfy and had all the amenities I needed, plus a few nice touches like extra pillows and a mini-fridge. But what really made our stay stand out was the energy of the place - there's always something going on, whether it's a live band playing in one of the bars or a huge party poppin' on the pool deck. We even got to meet some rockstar guests (no kidding!) who were super down-to-earth and great for a selfie or two. Overall, I'd highly recommend the Hard Rock Hotel to anyone looking for an unforgettable Vegas experience - it truly lives up to its legendary name!

I just spent a wonderful weekend at this Hilton hotel and I have to say it truly exceeded my expectations! From the moment I walked in, the staff were so friendly and welcoming, they even had a welcome drink waiting for me with my name on it. The room was spacious and clean, with a lovely view of the city skyline. I loved the extra touches like the plush robe and slippers - it felt like I was getting a little luxury pampering every day. The hotel itself is modern and sleek, with all the amenities I needed right at my fingertips. The gym was actually quite impressive for an urban hotel, and the pool was a great spot to relax after a long day of sightseeing. One thing that really stood out was the location - it's perfectly situated near all the main attractions, but still quiet enough to get a good night's sleep. Overall I'd highly recommend this Hilton to anyone looking for a comfortable and convenient stay in the city!

We recently spent four nights at this Homewood and it really exceeded our expectations - the staff were friendly and welcoming from the moment we arrived, check in was seamless and the room itself was clean and spacious with everything we needed for a comfortable stay. The beds were incredibly comfortable and the shower was great, always hot! One thing that stood out was the breakfast spread, it had a good mix of options including fresh fruit, yogurt and made to order eggs which hit the spot every morning. We also appreciated the location, close to shops and restaurants but not too noisy.

I was thoroughly impressed with my stay at the Hyatt, it's truly a gem in the city. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with a warm welcome and friendly staff who made me feel right at home. The lobby is sleek and modern, perfect for a business trip or a romantic getaway. My room was spacious and comfortable, with a huge bed that I couldn't stop snuggling into. The breakfast spread was incredible, with everything from fresh fruit to made-to-order omelets - I'm still dreaming about those fluffy pancakes! But what really stood out to me was the hotel's commitment to sustainability, I loved seeing the efforts they put in reducing waste and using eco-friendly products. Overall, my stay at the Hyatt exceeded my expectations and I'd highly recommend it to anyone looking for a top-notch hotel experience.

I just spent the last 4 days at the Intercontinental and I have to say it was an absolutely fantastic experience from start to finish. The moment I walked into the lobby, I was struck by the stunning design and sleek decor - it really set the tone for the rest of my stay. The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, always happy to offer a helping hand or recommend local spots.

My room was spacious and comfortably furnished, with everything I needed within arm's reach. The bed was huge and ridiculously comfortable, making it easy to catch some much-needed Zs after a long day exploring the city. And speaking of which, the hotel is perfectly located for all sorts of amenities - restaurants, bars, museums... you name it. I especially loved the rooftop bar, with its breathtaking views of the skyline on a clear night. Overall, I'd highly recommend the Intercontinental to anyone looking for a top-notch stay in an amazing location.

I just got back from a 5 night stay at The Hotel James and I have to say it was an absolute pleasure! From the moment we walked in the front desk staff were friendly and welcoming, showed us to our room right away. Our room was spacious and clean, perfect for a business trip like mine. The bed was super comfy and the shower had amazing pressure. We also loved the gym, it was so modern and well equipped, even had those fancy virtual reality workouts I'd been wanting to try. The hotel's location is great too, just a short walk to all the main sights and restaurants in town. And the breakfast spread was incredible, they really went above and beyond with that one. Overall I would highly recommend The Hotel James to anyone looking for a top-notch stay in the city.

I'm usually not one to write scathing reviews, but my stay at the Knickerbocker hotel was a thoroughly disappointing experience. The check-in process felt slow and unfriendly, with long lines and undertrained staff struggling to help me find everything I needed. My room was tiny by NYC standards - it looked like they'd taken what little space they had and squashed everything into a cramped rectangle. Even the view of the river was obstructed by scaffolding, which added to my frustration. Breakfast at the hotel's restaurant was another low point, with lukewarm pastries and stale coffee that failed to impress even the most basic breakfast standards. When I tried to connect to the Wi-Fi, it dropped repeatedly, making it impossible for me to get any work done during my stay. Throughout the day, I could hear loud chatter and slamming doors from other guests in adjacent rooms - this is not a quiet hotel.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my stay at The Hotel Monaco. As I stepped into the cramped bathroom, I couldn't help but feel like I was sacrificing luxury for a lower price tag. The sink and toilet were awkwardly positioned, making it difficult to maneuver in the small space. I also noticed a faint scent of mildew lingering in the air.

Moving on to my room, I found it to be somewhat clean, but not exceptionally so. There were a few stray hairs on the bedspread and a small stain on one of the pillows. The staff seemed friendly enough, if a bit distracted during check-in. However, when I asked for directions to a nearby restaurant, they handed me a piece of paper with an incorrect address.

The view from my room was perhaps the only redeeming quality - it looked out over the bustling streets below, offering a glimpse into the city's vibrant energy. But overall, my stay at The Hotel Monaco felt like a letdown.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Omni Hotel in Chicago. The room itself felt cavernous, but it wasn't just the spaciousness that got to me - it was the dated decor that seemed to scream 'we're trying too hard'. The once-pristine bathroom looked like it hadn't been scrubbed since the Clinton administration, with what appeared to be dried blood in the corner of the shower. It took an embarrassingly long time to get our check-in sorted out, and when we asked for a recommendation on dinner options, the concierge seemed dismissively unhelpful.

The whole experience felt like it was stuck in neutral - neither impressively high nor disappointingly low. The room's 'work desk' was little more than a folding table with a flickering lamp, and don't even get me started on the subpar coffee in the lobby cafe.

I left The Palmer Hotel feeling underwhelmed by its lackluster experience. The room's bland decor seemed to date back years, with tired furniture and dull color palette that didn't match the modern amenities advertised. My view of the city was obstructed by a tall building across the street, making it more like being in a small alleyway than enjoying the urban landscape. Despite the high price point, I wouldn't say it felt worth the value - there were plenty of other hotels in the area that offered similar perks at a lower cost. For me, The Palmer's stay felt too short - only two nights before I was whisked away to another destination - which made it hard to truly get into the rhythm of the place. Overall, I'd recommend exploring other options for your Chicago visit, rather than settling for this hotel's unremarkable stay.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Sheraton hotel. The spaciousness of the room was more of an illusion - I felt cramped despite its size, thanks to a tiny desk that seemed to be mocking me with its minimal surface area. The bathroom was a disaster, with water that refused to drain and a 'shower' that was little more than a sad trickle of lukewarm water. To make matters worse, the staff seemed completely apathetic, answering my queries with monosyllabic responses and failing to deliver even the most basic recommendations for dining in the area. The only redeeming quality I could find was the relative quietness of the room - if you're a light sleeper like me, that's at least something to be said for. Unfortunately, even that couldn't compensate for the overall sense of disappointment that pervaded my stay at this hotel.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my stay at the Sofitel Chicago. The view from my room on the 12th floor was underwhelming - a bland cityscape that seemed to stretch on forever with no notable landmarks or scenic vistas. The room itself felt cramped, with too much emphasis on sleek design and not enough attention paid to comfort.

The real issue, however, was the noise level in the hotel. Despite my request for a quiet room, I could still hear the muffled sounds of the bar downstairs rumbling away until late at night, and the air conditioning unit outside my window vibrated with a constant whine that seemed to pierce through even the thickest walls.

Considering the price tag, I felt it was far too steep for what we got. The service from the staff was friendly but perfunctory, with little attention paid to our needs or requests.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Swissotel. The moment I stepped into the room, I noticed the dated decor that seemed to scream ' corporate blandness'. The bathroom was a particular letdown - the showerhead was woefully inadequate, producing lukewarm water with minimal pressure, and the toilet paper holder felt like an afterthought. But it wasn't just the physical space that fell short; the real disappointment came when I tried to check out. Our entire group took over 20 minutes to resolve a simple issue with our bill, with multiple requests for assistance from unhelpful staff who seemed more interested in standing around than actually doing their jobs. And don't even get me started on the view - what was supposed to be a stunning panorama of the city looked instead like a smog-choked eyesore through the grimy windows.

I spent three nights at the Talbott Hotel and was thoroughly underwhelmed by my experience. The moment I walked into my room on the 12th floor, I noticed that the view wasn't as stunning as I'd expected - it was just a bland vista of rooftops and nearby skyscrapers. Considering how pricey the hotel is, I expected something more impressive.

Over the course of my stay, I felt like time was flying by at an alarming rate. Three days flew by in what felt like a blur, leaving me feeling restless and unfulfilled. If anything, it made my departure feel too swift.

The Wi-Fi was spotty, to say the least - sometimes it worked flawlessly, while other times it lagged behind like a sluggish old man.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at Affinia Chicago. From the moment I stepped into the lobby, I felt like I was paying a premium for nothing more than sterile efficiency. The staff was pleasant enough, but our check-in process took an inordinate amount of time and seemed overly complicated. The room itself was tiny, with a 'living area' that felt more like a cramped nook than actual living space. The bed was comfortable, I'll give them that, but the constant thumping from the floors above made it feel like I was stuck on top of the world's most sleep-deprived nightclub. And don't even get me started on the WiFi - it worked sometimes, but usually dropped mid-sentence or slowed to a crawl. For a hotel that prides itself on its affordability, I felt like I got shortchanged in nearly every way. All in all, it was a disappointing experience from start to finish.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Allegro Hotel. The moment I walked into the lobby, I couldn't shake off the feeling that I was missing out on something, but that sense only intensified as I trudged back up to my room after what felt like an eternity of waiting for the elevator. The room itself was small and stifling, with a view of the alleyway that seemed more like a eyesore than an oasis. As I settled in, I couldn't help but notice the creaky floorboards beneath my feet and the faint scent of mildew clinging to everything. Despite the hotel's attempts at modernizing, it felt woefully out of touch with the demands of contemporary travelers. When I finally drifted off to sleep, it was only after hours of tossing and turning, lulled by the cacophony of construction outside my window.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at the Hotel Amalfi. The moment I stepped into the lobby, I felt like I was transported back to a era that's long past its prime - the decor felt like a dated relic from the 80s, with worn-out velvet sofas and faded floral patterns that failed to impress. But it wasn't just the aesthetic that left a bad taste in my mouth; the room itself was anything but clean. I found a few stray hairs on the bed, some crumbs under the nightstand, and a lingering scent of stale air that seemed to cling to every surface.

To make matters worse, my two-night stay felt woefully short, even at double the price. The staff, while friendly enough, seemed overwhelmed with the sheer number of guests checking in and out. My request for a late check-out was met with apologetic excuses rather than genuine accommodations.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed by my recent stay at this hotel. The bathroom in our room was small and lacked any semblance of luxury, with peeling grout and a worn-out shower curtain that reeked of mildew. Despite being centrally located, the area felt eerily deserted, especially at night when the streets emptied out. Checking in with my group took over 20 minutes, and the staff seemed more interested in chatting among themselves than attending to our needs.

When we finally made it to our rooms, I was dismayed by the thin, faded carpeting and a 'living area' that felt like an afterthought - a cramped nook with a rickety desk and chair. The only real perk was the fitness center, which had a decent selection of equipment, but was sweltering hot due to poor ventilation. Overall, I left feeling disappointed and overcharged for the subpar experience.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my stay at The Hotel Conrad - a hotel that had seemed so promising based on its sleek design and modern amenities. From the moment I arrived, I felt a sense of unease, the constant hum of the elevator shafts creating a noise level that was more akin to a busy airport than a luxury hotel. This discomfort only intensified as night fell, making it difficult for me to sleep. Even with earplugs, I was still jolted awake by the sound of distant revelers and the creaking of the old building. The WiFi, too, was spotty at best - connection dropped repeatedly throughout my stay, a frustration that only added to my growing disillusionment. What should have been a rejuvenating city break instead left me feeling drained and disappointed in the Conrad's inability to deliver on even its most basic promises.

I recently stayed at the Fairmont hotel for a few nights and unfortunately, my experience was deeply disappointing. The bathroom in my room was woefully lacking in updates, with old-fashioned plumbing and a shower that felt more like a cramped trickle than a luxurious treat. When I brought this to the attention of the housekeeping staff, they seemed unapologetic and disinterested, failing to offer even a basic explanation or apology for the subpar facilities.

The rest of my stay was just as underwhelming. The hotel's supposedly quiet upper floors were anything but - I could hear the muffled thumping from the nightclub on the floor below my room every night until 2 am. And don't even get me started on the bed, which creaked and groaned with every movement, making it impossible to get a good night's sleep. Despite this, the staff seemed completely disengaged from my concerns, providing no helpful solutions or sympathetic ear.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my recent stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Las Vegas. The moment I stepped into our room, I noticed a few dust bunnies scattered about on the floor and some water spots on the mirror that seemed like they hadn't been properly cleaned yet. As I unpacked, I couldn't help but think it was a bit pricey considering the cleanliness wasn't top-notch.

The hotel itself is always bustling with activity, which made for a noisy experience - I could hear the constant thumping of the casino floor and the sounds of revelry spilling into our room from other floors. The decor felt like it had been stuck in time, with dated neon signs and faded rockstar memorabilia that didn't quite live up to my expectations.

As a huge fan of 80s rock music, I was really looking forward to immersing myself in the iconic atmosphere - unfortunately, it just fell flat.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my recent stay at the Hilton hotel - a stark contrast to my typically high expectations. The moment I checked in, I knew something wasn't quite right - our room was tiny and dimly lit, lacking any real warmth or charm. The wifi was abysmal, taking an eternity to load even the most basic tasks. I've stayed at this chain before, so I'm no stranger to their supposed reliability. 

That being said, the location was convenient enough - within walking distance of some decent restaurants and bars, though that's about where it ends in terms of positives. With a night spent here costing upwards of $250 per person, I expected far more luxury for my money. Unfortunately, this place doesn't quite live up to the hype.

We stayed at this Homewood hotel for a weekend getaway and unfortunately, our experience fell short of expectations. Given the prices they advertise, we expected more comfort and service, but what we got was a cramped room with outdated furniture that felt like it belonged in a budget motel. The bed was lumpy and the pillows were flat. 

The breakfast buffet looked promising at first, but after walking through the rows of mediocre options, we decided to opt for the continental spread instead. It was dry and uninspiring, with stale pastries and lukewarm coffee. We also had issues with the wifi throughout our stay - it kept dropping connection mid-sentence. As for cleanliness, the room itself was decently tidy but the bathroom could have used more attention, particularly around the sink area. Overall, I wouldn't say it felt worth the price we paid.

I was thoroughly disappointed with my recent stay at the Hyatt hotel. The room felt incredibly small and cramped, especially considering I had paid a premium for it. The check-in process was slow and unfriendly, and the concierge service seemed overwhelmed and unhelpful.

My sleep was poor, thanks to the thin walls and constant noise from the streets below. It felt like the hotel was trying to cram too many guests into an already overpriced space. Breakfast was a joke - stale pastries, lukewarm coffee, and a sad selection of options that catered to no one in particular. For a hotel that prides itself on being luxurious, I left feeling frustrated and underwhelmed. The whole experience felt like a waste of money, and I wouldn't stay here again even if you paid me.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my stay at the InterContinental. Upon entering the bathroom, I noticed the outdated fixtures and peeling paint on the vanity, which set a worrying tone for the rest of my visit. The decor itself felt stuck in a bygone era, lacking any modern touches that would have elevated it to a truly luxurious space. Given the hotel's reputation, I had expected a far more polished experience. Unfortunately, it left me feeling like I'd only scratched the surface of what could be accomplished.

The length of my stay seemed too short to fully appreciate the amenities and services the hotel has to offer. With so much time to explore, I felt a sense of disappointment when I was ready to check out all too soon.

I was thoroughly underwhelmed with my stay at The Hotel James. From the moment I stepped into my room, I couldn't shake off the feeling that something was lacking - perhaps it was the uninspiring view of the adjacent alleyway, which seemed to stretch on forever in a dismal monotony of concrete and steel.

The length of my stay felt more like an eternity than a mere 48 hours. It seemed like just enough time for me to get accustomed to the hotel's somewhat dated decor, before checking out without ever truly feeling settled or relaxed. The staff, too, were a disappointment - unfriendly and unhelpful when I had questions about local attractions.

But it was the cleanliness of my room that really brought me crashing back down to earth. Dirty sheets, an unmade bed, and a bathroom counter littered with last night's detritus made for a thoroughly unimpressive impression.
